title: Suriya and Trisha Reunite After 20 Years as Karuppu Crosses Rs 7 Crore in Pre-Sales
excerpt: RJ Balaji's courtroom action drama generates massive advance booking buzz ahead of May 14 release across global markets
body:
Suriya and Trisha Krishnan are back together on screen for the first time in two decades, and the Tamil film industry is paying attention. Their action drama Karuppu has crossed Rs 7.30 crore in worldwide pre-sales ahead of its May 14 release, making it one of the strongest advance booking openings for a Tamil film this year.

The numbers came fast. Within 19 minutes of bookings opening in Tamil Nadu, the film had already crossed Rs 10 lakh. By the 20-hour mark, Tamil Nadu pre-sales alone had breached Rs 1 crore, with worldwide advances climbing steadily past Rs 2 crore in the early hours before surging to the current Rs 7.30 crore figure.

**The Nostalgia Factor**

The last time Suriya and Trisha shared screen space was in the early 2000s, a period many Tamil cinema fans consider a golden era for the pair. That gap has created a reservoir of anticipation that director RJ Balaji — better known as a comedian and talk show host — is channeling into his most ambitious directorial project yet. Balaji has described Karuppu as a courtroom drama laced with action sequences and a mystery twist, a genre combination that Tamil cinema has explored successfully in recent years with films like Jai Bhim and Ponniyin Selvan.

Trisha's star has been on a remarkable upswing. After a string of critically acclaimed performances, she has cemented her position as one of South Indian cinema's most bankable leading women — a status that adds commercial weight to Karuppu's prospects.

**The Box Office Math**

Trade analysts are watching the advance numbers closely. For context, a Rs 7 crore-plus worldwide advance for a non-franchise Tamil film puts Karuppu in elite company. The film's performance in overseas markets — particularly the Middle East, North America, and Australia, where Tamil diaspora audiences are concentrated — will be a key indicator of its commercial ceiling. Early reports suggest steady traction in these territories, with premium shows in cities like Toronto, London, and Dallas already filling up.

For the estimated 700,000 Tamil-speaking Americans and the broader South Indian diaspora, Karuppu represents the kind of event release that draws first-day crowds to theaters in Edison, Fremont, and Plano — cities that have become reliable box office anchors for Tamil cinema abroad.

**What to Watch**

Opening day numbers on May 14 will determine whether Karuppu can convert advance buzz into sustained theatrical performance, with trade observers eyeing Rs 15-20 crore as the opening day target.
